title: Meet your dog
hint: A real dog, and the drawing we'll make of it.

title: Your pencils
hint: HB, 2H, 2B, and a dark pencil (4B or 6B, or any 3B-6B).
say: Four pencils today: a 2H for your very lightest construction, an HB for the main outline, a 2B for mid-tones, and a dark pencil -- 4B or 6B, or really any pencil from 3B to 6B -- for the darkest areas later on. Any pencil works; sharpen it only when you need a fine detail.

title: A blending stick, for later
say: A blending stick -- or stump -- blends small grey areas smoothly once the tone is built up. We'll get there in a few steps. For now, just know it's coming, along with a tissue and an eraser.

title: Feel your paper
hint: A little tooth helps the pencil grip.
say: Feel your own paper before you start. A little tooth helps the pencil grip -- that's what lets you build smooth, layered fur and tone later on.

title: The tilt axis
watchSay: Here, notice the very first line leans -- the whole head sits on a slant, not upright on the page. This whole outline uses an HB pencil, light and easy to adjust.
say: Start your own line with the same lean. Keep your HB light; these early marks are just for finding the angle.

card.title: The tilt axis
card.sub: The head sits on a slant, not upright.

title: The face as a faceted block
watchSay: What matters here is the big shape, not detail -- the face becomes one faceted block, like a cut strawberry, with straight planes instead of a curve.
say: Block your own head the same way: straight-sided facets, not a smooth oval. Add your own left ear as another flat plane.

card.title: The face as a faceted block
card.sub: Straight planes first, like a cut strawberry.

title: Ears and shoulders join the block
watchSay: Look at how the right ear becomes its own plane too, then the neck and shoulders -- the whole dog blocked in before anything gets refined.
say: Add your own right ear, then two lines down for the neck and shoulders. Keep every line straight for now.

card.title: Ears and shoulders join the block
card.sub: The whole dog blocked in before any detail.

title: Eye line, nose, and mouth placed
watchSay: Notice the eye line crosses straight through the centre, then the nose and mouth each get placed the same way -- all tangent lines, no curves yet.
say: Place your own eye line, nose, and mouth with straight marks. Leave real space between the eyes.

card.title: Eye line, nose, and mouth placed
card.sub: All three placed with straight tangent lines.

title: Inner and outer corners first
watchSay: Here, small tick marks find each eye's true corners before any curve begins -- inner corner, then outer.
say: Mark your own eye corners the same way, then let each eye become its own small frame.

card.title: Inner and outer corners first
card.sub: Small ticks mark each eye's true corners.

title: Eyelids: firm on top, light below
watchSay: What matters here is the contrast: the upper lid gets one firm, confident line, while the lower lid stays light and open -- that's what keeps the eye feeling alive.
say: Draw your own upper lid with one firm stroke, then keep the lower lid light. A heavy lower line makes the eye look puffy.

card.title: Eyelids: firm on top, light below
card.sub: A firm upper line; a light, open lower line.

title: Both eyes finished
watchSay: Notice both eyes now have real thickness, not just an outline -- a steady stopping point before anything gets refined further.
say: Take your time to finish this step. Continue when you're ready.

card.title: Both eyes finished, with thickness
card.sub: Take your time to finish this step.

title: Structure complete
hint: The whole dog is blocked in — good place to pause.
say: The whole dog is blocked in with straight lines, from the big shape down to the eyes. Good place to pause here if you'd like — next, we add quick detail to the eyes and ears.

title: Ear thickness, with small tangents
watchSay: This pass uses a light pencil -- 2H or HB -- small tangent lines only, nothing heavy yet. Notice each ear gets a little thickness: short straight tangents, not one long curve.
say: Add a few small tangents to your own ears' edges, the same light touch.

card.title: Ear thickness, with small tangents
card.sub: Short straight tangents, not one long curve.

title: A correction — and that's normal
watchSay: Watch the right ear get the same small tangents. Then notice a quick correction -- even a careful hand adjusts a line here. That's normal; kept tangents underneath can still look beautiful.
say: If one of your own tangents looks off, adjust it with a new line. No need to erase everything underneath.

card.title: A correction — and that's normal
card.sub: Kept tangents underneath can still look beautiful.

title: Nose and nostrils, still tangents
watchSay: Here, the nose and nostrils are built the same way: small straight tangents first. A tangent or an arc both work here -- there's no right or wrong, tangents are simply easier starting out.
say: Shape your own nostrils with small tangent lines. If an arc already feels natural to you, that works just as well.

card.title: Nose and nostrils, still tangents
card.sub: Tangents are simply easier starting out.

title: Eye detail begins
watchSay: Notice the eye work begins here -- remember, an eye isn't a line, it's a surface with real thickness, almost like a little dome. The same light pencil shapes it.
say: Begin shaping your own eye as a surface, not an outline -- give it that same gentle thickness.

card.title: Eye detail begins
card.sub: An eye is a surface, not a line.

title: Highlight, then the darkest pupil
watchSay: What matters here is order: the highlight goes in early, while there's still room for it -- then the darkest point of the pupil, then the greys around it. Put the highlight in early, or the eye ends up lifeless.
say: In your own eye, reserve the highlight first, then add the darkest pupil, then build the greys around it.

inset.label: Highlight first
inset.alt: The eye with a small reserved highlight

inset.label: Darkest pupil
inset.alt: The eye with the pupil darkened

inset.label: Then the greys
inset.alt: The eye with grey tone built up around the pupil

card.title: Highlight, then the darkest pupil
card.sub: Early, or the eye ends up lifeless.

title: The outer corner links to the lid
watchSay: Here, the outer corner gets strengthened until it connects with the eyelid above -- eye, lid, and brow bone all drawn together, like one family, never alone. The left eye gets the very same approach.
say: Strengthen your own outer corner until it meets the lid, then bring the left eye along the same way -- eye, lid, and brow together.

card.title: The outer corner links to the lid
card.sub: Eye, lid, and brow drawn together, like a family.

title: Both eyes finished
watchSay: Notice both eyes now carry real tone: inner and outer corners, a light lower lid, the highlight, the darkest pupil, and the greys around it -- the same order, for the second eye too.
say: Take your time to finish this step. Continue when you're ready.

card.title: Both eyes finished, with tone
card.sub: Take your time to finish this step.

title: Eyes and ears complete
hint: Eyes and ears have real tone — good place to pause.
say: Both eyes and ears now have real detail and tone. Good place to pause here if you'd like -- next, we build the light and dark across the whole face.

title: Tone begins, with a highlight saved
watchSay: Here, notice the very first layer of tone goes on with a 2H pencil -- a harder pencil that stays light on purpose, since the darkest marks come later. Even the nose gets a tiny highlight saved early, a spot of bare paper that will carry its shine all the way to the end.
say: Lay your own first layer of tone with a 2H, light across the whole head. Save a small highlight on your nose before tone covers it.

card.title: Tone begins, with a highlight saved
card.sub: A 2H pencil keeps the first layer light.

title: The nose becomes four planes
watchSay: What matters here is the nose as four clear planes -- top, front, left, and right -- not one rounded shape. Planes this clear are what make the whole nose feel solid.
say: Divide your own nose into the same four planes with straight lines, then let the nostrils go dark enough to hold their shape.

card.title: The nose becomes four planes
card.sub: Top, front, left, and right.

title: Bone and socket, one side at a time
watchSay: Look at how the work moves in close now -- one eye socket, one side of the forehead at a time. This dog's bones show clearly, so finding the socket and brow bone here is what keeps the whole structure accurate.
say: Work in close on your own eye socket too -- the hollow around the eye, and the bone of the brow above it.

card.title: Bone and socket, one side at a time
card.sub: Close work on one socket, then the other.

title: Eyes and nose relate
watchSay: Notice the eyes and nose coming forward together now, almost like one protruding block. Whiskers are already suggested beneath the nose too -- early, the same family of features, never alone.
say: Connect your own eyes down toward the nose bridge with light lines, and add a few whisker marks beneath the nose.

card.title: Eyes and nose relate
card.sub: Eyes, nose, and now whiskers -- never alone.

title: Nose bone to eye, cheek to neck
watchSay: Here, tone works around to the right side -- the nose bone linking eye and nose, with real bone thickness, not a thin wrinkle line. Then notice the cheek's shading carry straight down into the neck, one connected surface, no hard edge where they meet.
say: Build the same bone connection on your own right side, then let your cheek shading flow down into the neck the same way.

card.title: Nose bone to eye, cheek to neck
card.sub: Bones have thickness; surfaces turn, not jump.

title: Ear and head, plane by plane
watchSay: Notice the ear gets the same treatment now -- planes of tone, not outlines, to show what sits in front of the head and what falls behind it. The same light pencil follows the ear's own thickness all the way down.
say: Shade your own ear with planes of tone, the same light pencil, to show where it overlaps the head.

card.title: Ear and head, plane by plane
card.sub: Tone shows what's in front, and what falls behind.

title: The neck has its own direction
watchSay: Look at how the neck follows its own muscle direction now -- neck and shoulder as one plane, sitting in shadow since the light falls from the upper left.
say: Take your time to finish this step. Continue when you're ready.

card.title: Light and dark across the whole head
card.sub: Take your time to finish this step.

title: Tone complete
hint: Light and dark now shape the whole head — good place to pause.
say: Light and dark now wrap the whole head, with real bone structure underneath the surface. Good place to pause here if you'd like -- next, we go deep into just the eyes.

title: A softer, darker pencil arrives
watchSay: Here, notice the pencil change -- a softer 4B now, but only for the darks, and still used lightly. A soft pencil goes darker on its own, so there's no need to press. It lays down smooth, natural tone with hardly any visible strokes.
say: Pick up your own 4B and keep the same light touch. Let the softness of the pencil do the work, not your pressure.

card.title: A softer, darker pencil arrives
card.sub: 4B stays light at first -- it goes dark on its own.

title: The eye rebuilt: highlight, then pupil
watchSay: Notice the eye rebuilt in order -- the highlight restated first, then the darkest pupil around it, kept light, not dead. Tone graduates inward from the outline, and the corners are drawn slowly.
say: Rebuild your own eye the same way: highlight first, then the pupil around it, graduating inward.

card.title: The eye rebuilt: highlight, then pupil
card.sub: Corners drawn slowly, around the highlight.

title: Thickness, built slowly
watchSay: Here, thickness builds slowly -- the lower lid first, light and patient, then the upper lid's layered thickness building upward as well as inward. This kind of detail takes patience.
say: Build your own lid thickness slowly too: lower lid first, light, then the upper lid layered with more weight.

card.title: Thickness, built slowly
card.sub: Lower lid first, then the upper lid's weight.

title: The upper lid, like an umbrella
watchSay: What matters here is the upper lid -- like an umbrella, it shades the eyeball, so the eye sits under the lid instead of glaring bright. The left eye is finished now.
say: Take your time on this eye. Continue whenever it feels ready.

card.title: The upper lid, like an umbrella
card.sub: It shades the eye -- take your time here.

title: Between the eyes, with 2B
watchSay: Notice the pencil goes back to 2B between the eyes -- the eye never stands alone. Bone, muscle, and fold are drawn together: draw the top, look at the bottom; draw the left, look at the right.
say: Connect your own eyes with the same 2B before moving on -- bone and muscle drawn together, never isolated.

card.title: Between the eyes, with 2B
card.sub: The eye never stands alone.

title: Right eye: highlight, then pupil
watchSay: Same as the left eye -- highlight first, then the pupil, with the 4B back in hand.
say: Build your own right eye the same way. Take the time you need.

card.title: Right eye: highlight, then pupil
card.sub: Same as the left eye.

title: Right eye: thickness, the same way
watchSay: Same lid thickness as before -- lower lid, then the upper lid's weight, built slowly.
say: Give your own right eye the same patient thickness.

card.title: Right eye: thickness, the same way
card.sub: Lower lid, then the upper lid's weight.

title: Both eyes finished
watchSay: Notice both eyes now finished, each sitting under its own shading lid. A clear rest here before the next video.
say: Take your time to finish this step. Continue when you're ready.

card.title: Both eyes finished, with real depth
card.sub: Take your time to finish this step.

title: Eyes complete
hint: Both eyes are fully built now — good place to pause.
say: Both eyes are fully built now, with real depth and thickness. Good place to pause here if you'd like -- next, we go deep into the nose.

title: Follow the skeleton: eye bone to nose
watchSay: Here, a 4B pencil picks up again -- the same soft pencil from the eyes, still light. Notice the right eye's bone and the right ear's structure first, then the lower lid leads straight down into the nose. One area leads to the next; never jump.
say: Follow your own skeleton the same way: right eye bone, right ear, then straight down into the nose. Keep your 4B light.

card.title: Follow the skeleton: eye bone to nose
card.sub: One area leads to the next -- never jump.

title: Nostrils begin -- never filled solid
watchSay: Notice the nostrils stay open here, never filled in solid -- they go from very dark to light grey, or the nose loses its feeling of breathing. Imagine stroking the dog from its face down to its nose -- where does your hand travel? Follow the bones, not just the skin.
say: Shape your own nostrils the same way, dark to light grey, never solid -- let your hand follow the bones, the same path you'd stroke down to the nose.

card.title: Nostrils begin -- never filled solid
card.sub: Dark to light grey keeps it breathing.

title: Nostril value, dark to light
watchSay: Here, the value keeps building dark to light inside each nostril -- that gradient is what keeps the nose feeling soft and alive, never flat.
say: Build your own nostril value the same way -- dark at the opening, lightening as it turns.

card.title: Nostril value, dark to light
card.sub: That gradient keeps it soft, not flat.

title: The highlight, and reflected light saved
watchSay: What matters here is the highlight on the nose, and the reflected light saved around the nostrils -- that saved light is what makes the nose feel real.
say: Save your own highlight and the reflected light around your nostrils before anything covers them.

card.title: The highlight, and reflected light saved
card.sub: Saved light makes the nose feel real.

title: The nose finishes with 4B
watchSay: Notice the nose finishing now, still with the same 4B -- rich, dark values built up slowly, layer by layer.
say: Finish your own nose the same way, layering slowly with the 4B until it feels solid.

card.title: The nose finishes with 4B
card.sub: Rich values, layered slowly.

title: The blending stump arrives
watchSay: Here, the blending stump arrives -- loaded with graphite, it becomes a soft grey pencil of its own. No stump at home? A tissue rolled to a point, or a cotton swab, works just as well.
say: Reach for your own blending stump now -- or a rolled tissue or cotton swab if you don't have one.

card.title: The blending stump arrives
card.sub: No stump? A rolled tissue or cotton swab.

title: How to blend, three points
watchSay: What matters here is how to blend: use it like a pencil, with light pressure -- the result matches your strokes, only softer. Follow the direction of your strokes, never against them. Start slightly firmer, then lighten, to make a gradation. Watch it carry tone from the eyes down to the nose.
say: Blend your own tone the same way: light pressure, following your strokes, firmer to lighter.

card.title: How to blend, three points
card.sub: Light pressure, with your strokes, firm to soft.

title: The stump joins nose to face
watchSay: Notice the stump joins the nose to the face now, for one natural transition -- it's used all the way to the end.
say: Take your time to finish this step. Continue when you're ready.

card.title: The nose, softly blended into the face
card.sub: Take your time to finish this step.

title: Nose complete
hint: The nose is fully built now — good place to pause.
say: The nose is fully built now, with soft gradients and a natural blend into the face. Good place to pause here if you'd like -- next, we go deep into the mouth and neck.
